source.name: Bearfolk
source.heading: Bearfolk Traits and Shadowborn Bearfolk
sourceDistinctions: The book presents the base Bearfolk and Shadowborn in the same entry. Cloak of Night belongs to Shadowborn. Halla uses that complete profile.
source.catalogStatus: Fill existing indexed publication. No duplicate species row needed.

source.name: Bladeling
sourceDistinctions: The playable profile is labeled Bladeling Characters on printed p. 117, distinct from the adjacent monster stat blocks.
Razor Storm is a minor action and targets each creature in the burst. Use care around allies.
The Improved Razor Storm feat can replace the base power. Varik uses the original.

source.name: Centaur
source.heading: Centaurs As Characters
source.previousCatalogCoverage: Matching SRD monster row. This addition supplies the playable profile.
source.distinction: The SRD player bullet gives double Medium carrying capacity even though general Large quadruped rules give a different multiplier. This version uses the specific player bullet.

source.name: Cervan
source.sourceHeading: Chapter 1, Welcome to the Wood, Cervan traits
source.sourceDistinction: The player trait on p. 23 requires over half of current remaining HP from an attack. The separate Cervan Priest NPC on p. 193 uses equal to half or more. Grove and Pronghorn occupy one canonical profile here.

source.name: Corvum
source.coverage: Local rules and one original 2014-compatible NPC for the existing catalog index row. The subraces remain options under one species profile.
source.rulesDistinction: Use the original fixed ability increases and falling-only Glide. The separately published 2024 player update is outside this entry.

source.name: Daelkyr Half-Blood
sourceDistinctions: Symbiont Mastery adds 2 host HP per attachment and +4 to conflict saves, with no automatic bypass of Ego.
The throwing scarab provides one shard per round and no separate attack while attached. The damage dice follow the weapon entry and sample rogue.
The crawling gauntlet supplies a natural claw using host stats. Its standalone stat block is separate from the attached benefit.
source.portraitForm: Lysa Fenwick, an original Daelkyr Half-Blood scout with a throwing scarab

source.name: Darakhul
source.heading: Darakhul Traits, Bearfolk Heritage and Shadow Goblin Heritage
sourceDistinctions: The two heritages printed here are Bearfolk and Shadow Goblin. The book points readers to Tome of Heroes for further choices.
Keep the player creature type Humanoid and the susceptibility to undead effects. Do not inherit undead NPC stat-block immunities.
source.catalogStatus: Fill existing indexed publication. No duplicate species row needed.

source.name: Deva
sourceDistinctions: PHB2 p. 8 gives 1d6 for the baseline racial power. Auspicious Lineage is a separate option and Selian does not take it.
Astral Majesty is checked against the attacker’s bloodied status.

source.name: Disembodied
sourceDistinctions: The original 2021 player rules differ from the modular heritages in the revised D&D Beyond Player’s Guide.
The legacy Player Pack separately uses the printed title The Disembodied. The canonical name here follows the revised catalog name and keeps the 2021 book variant distinct.

source.name: Doppelganger
sourceDistinctions: The Monster Manual prints this option under Doppelganger. The Eberron Player’s Guide identifies it as the related Changeling and gives that later profile its own rules. The January 2010 updates use Changeling for the player race in Eberron feat references.
The gloss on p. 280 supplies the duration, equipment, and opposed impersonation rules.

supportingSources.title: Dungeon Master’s Guide (4e), NPC Design Steps
Player’s Handbook (4e), class and equipment rules
January 2010 official rules update, Eberron Player’s Guide

source.name: Dragonborn
source.heading: Dragonborn Lineage Traits
source.scope: Adds a playable Labyrinth Worldbook profile. Existing encounter monsters and playable Dragonborn printings have different source scopes.
decisions: The bonus-action breath offers a line or cone on each use, uses a CON-based DEX save, and includes void necrotic and yellow radiant ancestry choices.
The ancestry sentence names Natural Adaptation, but the section prints only the breath, hide, and sight effects. No inferred fourth trait.

source.name: Dreamer
sourceDistinctions: The original 2021 player rules differ from the modular heritages in the revised D&D Beyond Player’s Guide.

source.name: Gallus
source.coverage: Local rules and one original 2014-compatible NPC for the existing catalog index row. The subraces remain options under one species profile.
source.rulesDistinction: Use the original fixed ability increases and falling-only Glide. The separately published 2024 player update is outside this entry.

source.name: Gearforged
source.heading: Gearforged Lineage Traits
source.scope: Adds the playable Labyrinth Worldbook Gearforged.
decisions: Hybrid Humanoid keeps the Humanoid type and adds specific benefits.
The chassis sets size; an Upgrade is a separate choice. Always Armed text uses willingly in its disarming restriction.

source.name: Genasi
sourceDistinctions: Early 4e Realms rules use five manifestations and fixed +2 Strength, +2 Intelligence.
Each manifestation grants its own benefits and power. The Extra Manifestation feat can add another choice.
Avarra is a firesoul with the printed Firepulse immediate reaction. The published rules update removed the requirement to rest before a recovered swordmage can regain Warding.
The August 2012 compilation limits Promise of Storm bonus damage to hits by lightning or thunder attacks.

source.name: Githyanki
sourceDistinctions: This is the playable-with-permission trait on p. 277. The Warrior’s encounter statistics and powers in the monster entry are separate.

supportingSources.title: Dungeon Master’s Guide (4e), NPC Design Steps
Player’s Handbook (4e), class and equipment rules

source.name: Githzerai
sourceDistinctions: PHB3 gives 4e Iron Mind as a defense interrupt and ties the shift to second wind.

source.name: Gnoll
sourceDistinctions: The source is the original p. 277 player option, with Blood Fury. Dragon 367 presents a separate, later Gnoll player profile.

supportingSources.title: Dungeon Master’s Guide (4e), NPC Design Steps
Player’s Handbook (4e), class and equipment rules

source.name: Hedge
source.sourceHeading: Chapter 1, Welcome to the Wood, Hedge traits
source.sourceDistinction: The base quill AC and Curl Up AC are separate formulas. The original spell recharge is a short or long rest.

source.name: Hound Archon
source.heading: Hound Archons As Characters
source.previousCatalogCoverage: Matching SRD monster row. This addition supplies the playable profile.
source.distinction: SR and the aura save DC follow the player section. The ordinary archon combat entry has a fixed DC for its example. Teleport has a self and object limit.

source.name: Janni
source.heading: Jann As Characters
source.previousCatalogCoverage: Matching SRD monster row. This addition supplies the playable profile.
source.distinction: The unarmored player speeds are 30 ft. and fly 20 ft. The monster example shows 20 ft. and fly 15 ft. because it wears chainmail.

source.name: Jerbeen
source.sourceHeading: Chapter 1, Welcome to the Wood, Jerbeen traits
source.sourceDistinction: Take Heart requires proximity, sight, and hearing of a qualifying ally. Team Tactics grants the ordinary Help action, with its normal combat conditions.

source.name: Kalashtar
sourceDistinctions: Eberron’s 4e Kalashtar uses two-way telepathy with a creature that has a language inside 5 squares and line of sight.
Dual Soul offers a start-of-turn save against each dazing or dominating effect, with no end-of-turn retry on failure.
Bastion of Mental Clarity can change a Will attack’s result by interrupting it.

source.name: Karsite
source.evidence: The sample warrior’s DC 12 includes Ability Focus. The player trait starts at DC 10 + Charisma modifier.
source.catalogStatus: Missing playable profile at batch baseline.

source.name: Kobold
sourceDistinctions: This is the original Shifty at-will action on p. 278. Later Kobold player options use their own powers and are separate publications.

supportingSources.title: Dungeon Master’s Guide (4e), NPC Design Steps
Player’s Handbook (4e), class and equipment rules

source.name: Laneshi
sourceDistinctions: The original 2021 player rules differ from the modular heritages in the revised D&D Beyond Player’s Guide.

source.name: Lizardfolk
source.heading: Lizardfolk As Characters
source.previousCatalogCoverage: Matching SRD monster row. This addition supplies the playable profile.
source.distinction: The original PC entry uses checks to swim and gives no separate swim speed. The stat block includes a shield's Swim penalty and uses Multiattack on its sample bite.

source.name: Luma
source.coverage: Local rules and one original 2014-compatible NPC for the existing catalog index row. The subraces remain options under one species profile.
source.rulesDistinction: Use the original fixed ability increases and falling-only Glide. The separately published 2024 player update is outside this entry.

source.name: Lumi

additionalSources.name: Official Monster Manual III errata, July 2006

source.evidence: The official errata adds Extraplanar to the two published Lumi stat blocks. The base player traits remain on p. 99. Disrupt undead is a ranged touch attack with no save in the revised SRD, despite the printed parenthetical DC.
source.catalogStatus: Missing playable profile at batch baseline.

source.name: Mapach
source.sourceHeading: Chapter 1, Welcome to the Wood, Mapach traits
source.sourceDistinction: Temporary tools are single-use, and other temporary items generally endure for an hour. Materials and the durability of repairs remain GM calls.

source.name: Maug

additionalSources.name: Shadowdale: The Scouring of the Land (2007), p. 37, 3.5 Maug class example

source.evidence: The printed player paragraph gives class level +5 as ECL, corresponding to two retained construct HD and LA +3. The official 3.5 booklet identifies damage reduction and construct construction costs as its Fiend Folio changes. Shadowdale p. 37 confirms the 3.5 Construct traits, class scaling, and printed DC 18.
source.catalogStatus: Missing playable profile at batch baseline.

source.name: Minotaur
sourceDistinctions: Inspected the p. 10 scan visually. Paragon damage is 2d6 despite one text layer reading 1d6.
The PHB3 player option specifies Medium size. Brann adds the normal charge bonus to Goring Charge and uses the race-specific flat number in place of normal level/proficiency math.

source.name: Mul
sourceDistinctions: Born of Two Races is a choice for feat prerequisites.
Incredible Toughness uses no action at the start of the Mul’s turn. It explicitly lists four conditions alongside ongoing damage.
Daro shows a fighter able to act after ending a stun.

source.name: Nerra
source.pages: 127–130, Nerra Characters on pp. 128–129 and Varoot stat block on p. 130
source.evidence: The published ECL example is Varoot Rogue 1 at ECL 4, so it replaces its one outsider HD with the first class level. The print-era weapon sidebar calls shard weapons +2 wounding weapons. This build uses the revised core wounding property and names disguise self as the revised equivalent of change self.
source.catalogStatus: Missing playable profile at batch baseline.

source.name: Ogresh
sourceDistinctions: The original 2021 player rules differ from the modular heritages in the revised D&D Beyond Player’s Guide.

source.name: Pixie
source.heading: Pixies As Characters
source.previousCatalogCoverage: Matching SRD monster row. This addition supplies the playable profile.
source.distinction: The character list grants the spell-like abilities and does not list the monster's optional special arrows. The original NPC uses ordinary arrows and the LA +4 profile.

source.name: Quickstep
source.heading: Quickstep Traits
sourceDistinctions: Startling Speed imposes attack disadvantage after movement. The effect is limited to attack disadvantage. Character level sets the daily round count. The corrected printing gives Small size.
The book grants Fey Ancestry and leaves the creature type implicit in the player traits. Humanoid is the table ruling for this example.
source.catalogStatus: Fill existing indexed publication. No duplicate species row needed.

source.name: Raptor
source.coverage: Local rules and one original 2014-compatible NPC for the existing catalog index row. The subraces remain options under one species profile.
source.rulesDistinction: Use the original fixed ability increases and falling-only Glide. The separately published 2024 player update is outside this entry.

source.name: Ratatosk
source.heading: Ratatosk Racial Traits, Ekorre and Tradvakt
sourceDistinctions: Both Ekorre and Tradvakt share the printed Strength reduction and Dexterity increase. Ekorre differ in size, weapon handling and magic. Tradvakt use Constitution for War Chatter.
Grounded Celestial is a targeting rule. It does not change the character’s Humanoid type.
source.catalogStatus: Fill existing indexed publication. No duplicate species row needed.

entries.name: Sapopova
entries.publication: Tales of the Valiant Player's Guide 2 Preview

source.name: Sapopova
source.publication: Tales of the Valiant Player's Guide 2 Preview
source.heading: Sapopova Lineage Traits
source.scope: One playable lineage with Frogkin and Toadfolk equipment and movement choices. Source is the full lineage treatment in the publisher’s preview.
decisions: The Frogkin rules remove the launch run for long jumps. The Toadfolk rules permit three Tiny items while maintaining speech and state the launched-object range and damage formula.

source.name: Satyr
source.heading: Satyr Lineage Traits
source.scope: Adds a Black Flag playable Satyr profile. The existing D&D options and Black Flag encounter monster have distinct mechanics.
decisions: Bounding Leap costs a reaction after a melee or unarmed hit. The 1d8 horns use STR or DEX by choice at creation.
Black Flag condition resistance grants advantage on checks and saves to avoid or end that condition. See BFRD p. 250 or Resistant in the Monster Statistics chapter.

source.name: Shadow Goblin
source.heading: Shadow Goblin Traits
sourceDistinctions: The playable Stink Eye is an action and affects only the next qualifying roll. The chieftain stat block later in the book uses a different bonus-action version.
source.catalogStatus: Fill existing indexed publication. No duplicate species row needed.

source.name: Shardmind
sourceDistinctions: The six-hour extended rest is on p. 13. Lack of a need to sleep does not itself give immunity to every sleep effect.
Shard Swarm applies combat advantage before teleporting.

source.name: Strig
source.coverage: Local rules and one original 2014-compatible NPC for the existing catalog index row. The subraces remain options under one species profile.
source.rulesDistinction: Use the original fixed ability increases and falling-only Glide. The separately published 2024 player update is outside this entry.

source.name: Syderean
source.heading: Syderean Lineage Expanded: Spellborn
source.scope: One canonical Syderean species record. This profile uses the Spellborn Natural Adaptation alongside base lineage traits from the Player’s Guide.
decisions: Energy Form adds physical resistance and restraint immunity during transformation. The selected elemental type replaces damage for one attack or spell on each of the character’s turns, and grants no matching elemental resistance by itself.

source.name: Thri-kreen
sourceDistinctions: Use low-light vision from the original 4e printed rules.
Multiple Arms changes the action economy once per turn. It grants no extra attack or wielded item slots.
Thri-Kreen Claws is a single minor action with one to three adjacent enemy targets.

source.name: Vulpin
source.sourceHeading: Chapter 1, Welcome to the Wood, Vulpin traits
source.sourceDistinction: Printed p. 30 grants Intelligence-based spells at levels 1, 3, and 5. Ambush prey is defined on printed p. 49. The Dexterity-save modifier adds to the normal roll.

source.name: Warforged
sourceDistinctions: Use the p. 279 player text. The p. 261 Warforged Soldier has a different Resolve amount, and the Eberron Player’s Guide uses a different racial power.
The death-save bullet allows taking a 10. Its negative-HP wording is read alongside the general negative-bloodied rule in the Player’s Handbook, p. 295, if the DM uses dying rules for this NPC.

source.name: Wechselkind
sourceDistinctions: The original 2021 player rules differ from the modular heritages in the revised D&D Beyond Player’s Guide.
The 2021 Artificial Form explicitly uses the Humanoid creature type despite the doll's construction.

source.name: Wilden
sourceDistinctions: All three aspects are abilities of one race. Each extended rest sets which single encounter power is available. Briar begins with Hunter.
